# Roadmap, as a list

What Launchway does today and what is planned, in milestones marked Now, Next and Later. The same
items are drawn on the [roadmap](./public/roadmap.html). As of 2026-11-21.

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs/build-roadmap.mjs from docs/roadmap/roadmap.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Launchway is one place to host your code, build it, test it, scan it and deliver it, on servers you control or as a hosted service. It aims to be complete without being complicated: every task is a guided wizard, every capability is also in the API, the command line, the agent endpoint and Terraform, and the only things it needs are a database and Git. AI helps where you ask for it and stays off where you do not, and every run, change and approval is a durable record you can audit.

Order is by value, not a schedule, and plans change. An item is **available** only when it is on the
main branch, tested and documented. Launchway is not certified against any compliance standard;
compliance items provide controls and evidence.

## Available today

| Item | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| Pipelines as code | Typed YAML with steps, dependencies, run inputs, outputs passed between steps and loops, kept in Git next to the code they build. ([more](guide/pipelines.md)) |
| Flow control | Conditions on steps, retries with back-off, lanes that make runs take turns, run timeouts, and re-running from any step with what each step was given. ([more](reference/pipeline.md#when)) |
| Build caches | Dependencies kept between runs in the database, with entries a pull request can write but the default branch never reads. ([more](guide/build-caches.md)) |
| Triggers | Push, pull request (with target-branch filters, and newer pushes cancelling older runs), manual, schedule and webhook. ([more](guide/triggers.md)) |
| Shared libraries | Templates and scripts in their own repository, pinned by tag, branch or commit, with typed parameters. ([more](guide/libraries.md)) |
| Step resources | Each step is sized, with defaults per kind of step and a ceiling no step can pass, so one step cannot starve a cluster. ([more](reference/config-objects.md#step-resources)) |
| Configuration in the database | Projects, runner pools, environments, policies, models and more are objects in the database with history, audit and safe concurrent edits, never a file to hand-edit. ([more](guide/configuration.md)) |
| Four levels | Installation, organisation, unit and project, with names you choose and levels nobody uses kept out of sight. ([more](guide/configuration.md#levels)) |
| Guided setup wizards | First-run setup, connecting a repository, adding a runner, an environment, a policy or a verification step: plain questions, explained options, answers checked as you go. ([more](howto/setup-first-run.md)) |
| A guided interface | Six sections (Home, Projects, Deployments, Activity, Library, Settings), a Home page that says what to do next, and sections that appear only when there is something to show. ([more](demo.md)) |
| One capability, every interface | What the web UI does, the HTTP API, the command line and the agent endpoint do too, with a table in the build that fails when one falls behind. ([more](reference/interface-parity.md)) |
| High availability | Several servers on one PostgreSQL database with no leader; a run survives a server or a runner dying. SQLite for a single server. ([more](guide/high-availability.md)) |
| Signed releases and installers | Reproducible, signed release builds with SBOMs and provenance, deb and rpm packages and an install script for runners, and a runner-only Helm chart. The first published release is still to come. ([more](security/verify-downloads.md)) |
| Self-deploy | Launchway builds, tests and deploys itself through its own pipeline, with a way back in when it is down. ([more](howto/self-deploy.md)) |
| Quality gates | Lint, size, architecture, test and originality checks fail the build, so the code stays easy to change. ([more](development/quality-gates.md)) |
| GitOps with Argo CD | Deploy by Git commit, watch sync and health, control Argo Rollouts (promote, abort, retry), roll back, lock environments. ([more](guide/deployments.md)) |
| Applications view | The Argo CD applications a deploy runner has seen, shown with their status next to your environments. ([more](guide/deployments.md)) |
| Verification after a deploy | Checks on Prometheus, Loki, ClickHouse and OpenSearch with automatic abort or rollback; an optional model explains the verdict and never turns a failure into a pass. ([more](guide/verification.md)) |
| Container images | Rootless builds, scans, signatures, provenance and SBOMs, pushed to any OCI registry. ([more](guide/images.md)) |
| Approvals and protected environments | Approval steps; the person who started a run cannot approve its production deploy. ([more](guide/approvals-and-reruns.md)) |
| Policy gates | Rules pipelines cannot opt out of, at run start, before deploys and image pushes; report or enforce; audited, expiring waivers. ([more](guide/policies.md)) |
| Sign-in and access | OpenID Connect sign-in with groups, roles per project and environment, scoped API tokens and an audit trail. ([more](guide/access.md)) |
| Secrets that stay with runners | Pipelines hold references; runners read values from Vault, OpenBao, files or the environment, and mask them. ([more](guide/secrets.md)) |
| Security findings and SBOMs | Secret, code, dependency, licence and image findings (SARIF), new and fixed across runs, and a component search. ([more](guide/security-findings.md)) |
| Secure step execution | Non-root step pods under strict pod security; container and host executors; runners only connect outbound. ([more](security/trust-model.md)) |
| Runner identity and pools | Join tokens, a key per runner, pools scoped to projects, and allow-lists on the runner itself. ([more](guide/runner-identity.md)) |
| Test, coverage and HTML reports | Thirteen test formats, coverage with thresholds, flaky-test detection, history, and the tools' own HTML reports in a sandbox. ([more](guide/test-reports.md)) |
| Built-in artifact storage | Artifacts and hosted reports live in the database by default, so several servers need nothing else; S3 or a shared folder are optional. ([more](artifacts.md)) |
| AI models in steps | Optional hosted or local models for steps and failure explanations, with per-model token limits; keys never enter a step's container. ([more](guide/ai.md)) |
| An endpoint for agents | Agents validate pipelines, start and watch runs and diagnose failures with exactly the rights of the token they hold. ([more](guide/agents.md)) |
| Open source | Free software under the AGPL-3.0, with a commercial licence for those who cannot use it, and this documentation site with its roadmap. ([more](https://github.com/JK-Magic-Creations/launchway/blob/main/LICENSING.md)) |

## Milestone 1: Host your code and run your pipelines in one place (Now)

A team can keep its repositories in Launchway, review and merge there, and run every pipeline it has, with everything a hosted CI service offers and nothing else to install.

### Host your code

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Built-in Git hosting | In progress | Launchway stores your repositories and serves them over standard HTTPS, with storage designed so that no acknowledged push is ever lost. |
| Pull requests on the built-in host | Planned | Open, review, discuss and merge changes inside Launchway, with branch rules that block a merge until required checks pass. |
| Browse and search your code | Planned | History, blame, raw files, archives, permanent links and code search, so you rarely leave Launchway to read code. |
| Repository administration | Planned | Settings screens, maintenance tools and a trash from which a deleted repository can come back. |
| Issues and work items | Planned | Track work next to the code, import existing issues, and link every change to the reason for it. |
| Move your repositories in | Planned | Import repositories, issues and settings from another Git host, and keep a mirror back while you switch. |
| An acceptance suite for hosting | In progress | A written end-to-end suite that hosting must pass before it is called ready, so that switching is a tested step, not a leap. |
| A complete Git forge | Planned | Wiki, static pages, forks, large files, SSH access, time tracking and the rest of a hosted Git service, in order of value, with an interface that is better integrated than a stand-alone one. |

### Keep your Git host, if you prefer

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Every Git host, equally | Planned | First-class connections to every major Git host, including self-managed ones, with each one's limits stated plainly in the docs and the wizards. |
| Pull-request status everywhere | Planned | Report each run back to the pull request as a status and block a merge that does not pass, on the built-in host and on every connected one. |

### Pipelines that match what teams expect from hosted CI

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Conditions, retries, lanes and re-runs | Available | Run a step only when it should, retry what is flaky, make runs take turns, and re-run from any step. ([more](reference/pipeline.md#when)) |
| Warm builds with caches | Available | Keep dependencies between runs so builds start warm, with rules for who may read and write them. ([more](guide/build-caches.md)) |
| Flow control, part two | In progress | Services with readiness checks and logs, a runner and workspace of their own per step, approval quorums, and loops that tolerate chosen members. |
| Platform matrices | Planned | Run the same steps across operating systems and architectures from one definition. |
| Cloud sign-in per step | Planned | Each step proves its identity to a cloud with short-lived tokens, so no long-lived cloud keys are stored. |

### Move your existing pipelines over

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| A converter and a move-over guide | Planned | Bring pipelines written for other CI services across in waves, with a report of anything that needs a person. |

### Foundations that finish alongside

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Terraform provider | Planned | Every kind of setting managed as code, each new kind shipping with its resource, so nothing is reachable only by clicking. ([more](reference/config-objects.md#terraform)) |

## Milestone 2: Deeper pipeline power, and a way off self-hosted automation servers (Next)

Pipelines can be as dynamic as real code needs, and a team running an automation server can move its jobs without losing what it relies on.

### Write pipelines your way

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Custom steps in your own language | Planned | A step is a program in your repository with typed inputs, outputs and secrets, runnable and testable on its own, so pipeline logic is ordinary tested code. |
| Generated pipelines | Planned | A step can print more steps in any language; Launchway checks them against the same schema and policy and shows them on the run. |
| Expressions for conditions | Planned | A small typed expression language with no loops and no side effects, checked before the run; today's conditions keep working. ([more](reference/pipeline.md#when)) |
| Typed outputs between steps | Planned | A step declares what it passes on, and a reference to an output that does not exist fails before the run, not in the middle of it. |
| A browsable catalogue of templates and steps | Planned | Shared libraries pinned by tag already work; the catalogue lets you find, compare and update them from inside the product. ([more](guide/libraries.md)) |
| A triggers page | Planned | One page showing every trigger and exactly which pipelines it starts. |
| Event sources and container graphs | Planned | Start pipelines from message queues and buses, and lay steps out as a graph of containers. |
| Runners that keep themselves updated | Planned | Runners on VMs and on customers' machines update under your policy, so the fleet never drifts. |

### Design visually

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| A visual pipeline designer | Planned | Drag built-in and custom steps into place; it edits the same pipeline file as the text editor, so the two are views of one thing. |
| A drawing canvas and diagrams | Planned | Architecture diagrams drawn in Launchway beside generated ones and Mermaid, and a two-way sync with note-taking vaults. |

### Move off a self-hosted automation server

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| A verified gap analysis | Planned | A tested list of what teams rely on automation servers for (dynamic pipelines, extensions, agents anywhere) with a plan for each gap. |
| Import of existing jobs | Planned | Convert job definitions and shared libraries, with a report of what needs a person, and none of the file-first configuration or fragile plug-ins. |

## Milestone 3: Delivery and GitOps depth (Next)

See and control everything you run, whether it is an application in a cluster, a virtual machine or an image-based host, and deliver to it safely.

### Applications and rollouts

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Argo CD in depth | Planned | Application hierarchy views (app-of-apps and ApplicationSet trees) with status, sync, health, history and actions, ready health checks, and a hosted or your own Argo CD. ([more](guide/deployments.md)) |
| A single pane of glass | Planned | One fleet view of every application and every host: what runs where, its health, drift and evidence. |
| Weighted canaries and traffic control | Planned | Send a share of traffic, by client type, to a new version through the Gateway API or a service mesh, with mesh metrics as ready-made health checks. |
| Releases across services | Planned | Ship several services as one ordered, gated release with a promotion view across environments. |
| Post-deploy watch and incidents | Planned | Keep watching after release, roll back automatically, and tie incidents to the change that caused them. |

### Where it deploys

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Built-in Helm and Kubernetes deploys | Planned | Deploy and roll back without Argo CD; Argo stays first class for long-lived environments. |
| Preview environments | Planned | Every pull request or branch gets its own environment and address, tested and cleaned up on merge. |
| VM deploys | Planned | Roll a change across virtual machines in batches over SSH, with verification between batches. |
| Image-based hosts | Planned | Machines that are really images, built, signed, upgraded and rolled back like container images, with host setup done at first boot. |
| Machine images with Packer | Planned | Bake machine images in a pipeline and roll them through instance groups. |
| An infrastructure stack designer | Planned | Compose image, build and configuration blocks visually and have them turned into pipelines. |
| Cloud and serverless targets | Planned | AWS, Google Cloud and Azure, including serverless and managed instance groups, with no stored cloud keys. |

### Infrastructure as code

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Terraform and OpenTofu | Planned | Reviewed plans, applies that run only the reviewed plan, state kept and locked inside Launchway, and drift detection. |
| Ansible and Chef | Planned | Typed steps with per-host or per-node results and a check mode before apply. |

### Runtime configuration

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Feature toggles | Planned | A built-in toggle service that applications and agents read, per environment, with percentage and client-type rollouts. |
| Configuration, keys and toggles per zone | Planned | Manage settings and secrets together per zone and environment, for virtual machines and Kubernetes alike. |

### Change and insight

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Change management | Planned | Automatic change records with risk scores, freezes and approvals, with optional ServiceNow and Jira Service Management. |
| Delivery metrics and executive dashboards | Planned | Deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore, with drill-down to the runs behind each number. |
| Service reliability targets | Planned | Set targets for the services you run and see whether a release is spending the budget. |

## Milestone 4: A built-in registry (Later)

Images, Helm charts and other OCI artifacts stored beside the code, under the same permissions and policies.

### Registry

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| A built-in OCI registry | Planned | Store container images, Helm charts and other OCI artifacts in Launchway, passing the OCI conformance suite, with nothing else to run. |
| Retention that protects what runs | Planned | Clean up old images without ever deleting one that is deployed, and promote an image between environments by its digest. |
| Pull-through cache and image guard | Planned | Cache public images, and keep unchecked images away from sandboxed builds. |
| Any other registry, equally | Available | Pushing to any OCI registry works today and stays first class beside the built-in one. ([more](guide/images.md)) |

## Milestone 5: The software graph, with automated patching (Later)

One connected picture of code, dependencies, images and deployments, so you always know what runs where and can fix it safely.

### Know what you run

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Findings and SBOMs per run | Available | The starting point already works: findings and components recorded for every run. ([more](guide/security-findings.md)) |
| What is deployed where | Planned | Link every deployed image back to its commit, its components and its findings, including on hosts Launchway only observes. |
| Continuous scanning of what runs | Planned | Scan deployed software for new vulnerabilities and best-practice gaps, not only at build time. |
| Code search and code intelligence | Planned | Search symbols and references across repositories, and give people and agents the context they need. |

### Fix it safely

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Automated patching | Planned | Off by default and turned on per zone: updates open as changes, pass tests and change management, and roll out through Argo CD. |
| Built-in dependency updates | Planned | Keep common ecosystems' dependencies current, as ordinary reviewable pull requests. |

## Milestone 6: AI as an optional first-class helper (Later)

AI wherever it saves effort, always optional, always off until an administrator turns a purpose on, and never able to hide a failure.

### Today

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Models in steps and verification | Available | Hosted or local models in steps, with explanations of failures and verdicts that never override a failing check. ([more](guide/ai.md)) |
| Agents as users | Available | The agent endpoint gives agents the same permissions, limits and audit as any user. ([more](guide/agents.md)) |

### Next

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| A built-in model gateway | Planned | One endpoint that routes to any hosted or self-hosted model, with usage monitoring and easy switching of providers. |
| Spending limits | Planned | Budgets in money, per model, project and purpose, not only in tokens. |
| Context compression | Planned | Shrink what is sent to a model without losing file paths, line numbers or error codes, with every omission marked and the saving measured. |
| A protected path for regulated data | Planned | Use only models whose data-handling terms you have recorded, so that regulated projects never reach the wrong one. |
| Models that know Launchway | Planned | Optional models tuned on Launchway itself, runnable locally and never trained on customer data. |
| AI analysis as an optional rollback gate | Planned | Let a verification step use AI analysis of metrics and logs to trigger automatic rollback, off by default and able to require a person for production. |
| From a picture to a pipeline | Planned | Design a delivery visually and have AI help translate it into a pipeline you can read and edit. |

## Milestone 7: The hosted service, the public demo and enterprise controls (Later)

Use Launchway without running it, on a plan that follows your choices, with the controls enterprises and regulated teams ask for.

### Hosted service and demo

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Hosted service | Planned | Launchway as a service: sign-up, quotas, usage metering, a free tier, pay for use, every option on every plan, and data residency. |
| Runners on your machines | Planned | Runners on your own servers or clusters connect out to the hosted engine, so code and secrets never leave your network. |
| Sandboxed hosted runners | Planned | Each step in its own isolated machine, with no route to anything but the internet and firm quotas; the same profile available to any self-hosted server. |
| A public demo | Planned | A safe instance on the internet with realistic data anyone can explore, read-only at first. A local demo already runs from the quick start. ([more](demo.md)) |
| Organisations | Planned | Several organisations on one installation, isolated from each other, with the level names you choose. |

### Identity, audit and compliance

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Built-in accounts with MFA | Planned | Small teams without an identity provider still get secure sign-in with authenticator codes or passkeys. |
| Directory groups and custom roles | Planned | LDAP and Active Directory groups mapped to roles at each level, leavers removed automatically, and a view of who can do what, and why. |
| Tamper-evident audit and SIEM export | Planned | An audit trail nobody can quietly edit, streamed to your security tools. |
| Retention, legal hold and encryption at rest | Planned | Choose how long data is kept, prove deletion, and encrypt logs and artifacts with rotating keys; encrypted by default when hosted. |
| A compliance pack for PCI DSS and HIPAA | Planned | Policy templates and an evidence report that maps controls to requirements. It supports your compliance work and is not a certification. ([more](security/controls-and-compliance.md)) |

## Beyond delivery (Later)

Ideas that grow naturally from one connected platform. Planned, but behind everything above.

### Operate what you ship

| Item | Status | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud cost management | Planned | See what each service, team and environment costs to run, next to what it delivers. |
| Chaos testing | Planned | Deliberately break things in a pre-production environment as a pipeline step, and see whether verification notices. |
| A developer portal and service catalogue | Planned | A directory of every service with its owner, health, docs and deployments. |

## Throughout, not a milestone

- **Everything, without the mess.** Every feature uses the same objects, permissions, audit trail and policy point, and nothing switched off appears in the menus.
- **One way in, every way in.** A wizard for each task, with the same operation in the HTTP API, the agent endpoint, the command line and Terraform.
- **Only a database and Git.** Everything else is built in; outside integrations stay optional.
- **Boring upgrades.** One binary and a database, additive migrations, an older binary running on a newer schema, and rollback by image.
- **High availability and security are part of done.** A feature says what happens when a server, the database or a runner dies, and who may do what, before it merges.
- **Honest status.** An item is available only when it is merged, tested and documented. Order is by value and is not a schedule.
